messages:
elaine: heads-up — saw a save that passed the console linter but failed at runtime with a header-match collision. saving worked, but router returned 500s in staging. not sure if console validation is too permissive or runtime stricter. anyone seen this before? :facepalm:

tariq: can you paste the failing yaml? i can try to repro locally. i vaguely remember header tiebreakers being brittle when we have both exact and prefix matchers on same header.

elaine: pasted below — minimal repro extracted from customer config:
```yaml
routes:
  - id: route-a
    match:
      - header:
          name: x-tenant
          exact: "acme"
  - id: route-b
    match:
      - header:
          name: x-tenant
          prefix: "ac"
    overrides:
      response_timeout_ms: 5000
```
console saved this with no warnings. runtime errors show: "conflicting header matcher: duplicate key 'x-tenant'" and then 500.

kevin: hmm. console validation currently checks per-rule schema and then a shallow uniqueness check that only looks at (route id, header name) pairs. it doesn't consider matcher types (exact vs prefix) which our runtime treats as distinct but incompatible in routing index.

elaine: so runtime treats them as collision, console allows them because it thinks "same header name is fine if rules different". that mismatch is the problem.

kevin: think we have three paths: 1) strengthen console linter to enforce runtime collision rules 2) relax runtime to accept sorted precedence between exact/prefix 3) surface a preflight warning in console with a link to docs and let user opt-in.

elaine: option 3 is least disruptive short-term. but customer expectations — they expect save to be safe. i'd prefer console block on this until we can show deterministic precedence.

ui-bot: autovalidation: schema check passed. custom-lints: header-uniqueness -> WARNING (soft): "Different matcher types for header 'x-tenant' may conflict at runtime". (rule id: header-matcher-composition).

tariq: can we add a unit test in routing-config-linter that loads the runtime matcher-composition logic and runs against console linter output? if console rule mirrors runtime decision we avoid surprises.

kevin: yes. plan: add an integration harness that imports the runtime's matcher-indexer and run it against example yaml. if indexer errors, console linter should return an ERROR instead of WARNING. i'll draft a PR.

elaine: also adding a clear error message is key. right now runtime message is "duplicate key" which is opaque to users. can we map indexer error to something like: "Conflicting header matchers for 'x-tenant': exact vs prefix — choose one or split into separate routes with disjoint matchers"

kevin: agreed. will add translation layer in runtime and surface it up the stack so console can catch and show it too.

qa-bot: ran quick regression tests on staging after reverted console save to previous commit. routing e2e: 128/130 passed. two flakes unrelated (auth timeout). added test case for header exact+prefix collision -> expected: console-error and runtime-reject.

tariq: what about rollout UX? if we change console linter to ERROR, we need a migration path for saved configs currently live in Dedicated/Private customers. we should not break their dashboards mid-rollout.

kevin: good catch. we can add a versioned linter: configs with schema_version < 2026-02 keep permissive behavior, new saves validated strictly. also add a console warning banner for orgs with legacy configs when they open route authoring.

elaine: that sounds reasonable. timeline? we need the change gated behind a feature flag for 2 weeks before turning on org-wide.

kevin: i'll open PR with: 1) linter update + tests 2) runtime error translation 3) feature flag behind admin toggle. target: small canary next week, org-wide after 2 weeks pending fallout.

elaine: thanks. can someone add a short doc blurb for the console warning text and an example fix snippet we can show inline? i can write wording if you want.

tariq: i'll add the test fixtures for the harness. kevin, ping me on the PR for review.

kevin: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

elaine: ok closing loop here — created a follow-up ticket in #eng-releases to schedule canary and send heads-up to ops.
